claim: The founding act of the measured mind: sensation brought under a formula. Fechner's Maßformel is the first claim that inner life obeys an equation — the premise every later attempt to compute the mind inherits.
geplant: Selections from vol. I (the programme of psychophysics, Weber's law, the measurement formula) from the 1860 printing (Internet Archive elementederpsych001fech; vol. II 10255089). German with a working translation made for this site — the English translation of 1966 is in copyright and will not be consulted.

titel: Memory: A Contribution to Experimental Psychology (1885) — selections
claim: Learning becomes a curve: nonsense syllables, the savings method, forgetting as a lawful function of time. The learning curve that machine learning still plots begins here.
geplant: Selections from the Ruger/Bussenius translation of 1913 (Internet Archive memorycontributi00ebbiuoft), public domain; the German original of 1885 named beside it.

titel: Inquiries into Human Faculty and its Development (1883) — selections
claim: Association timed with a stopwatch, mental imagery surveyed by questionnaire, faces averaged into composite photographs — statistical portraits of the mind, a century before embeddings.
geplant: Selections from the first edition (Internet Archive inquiriesintohu00galtgoog): the association experiments, the imagery questionnaire, composite portraiture. Galton's role in founding eugenics is stated, not passed over.

claim: Intelligence becomes a factor: correlation, measurement error, and the general factor g extracted from the numbers. The mathematics of “how intelligent?” — the question later asked of machines.
geplant: The 1904 American Journal of Psychology paper, carried in selections from the original printing (Internet Archive jstor-1412107, JSTOR Early Journal Content).

titel: The Development of Intelligence in Children (1905–1911; Kite's English of 1916) — selections
claim: The intelligence test itself: graded tasks, norms, a scale. The instrument that made ‘measuring intelligence’ an operational question — the ancestral form of every benchmark.
geplant: Selections from Elizabeth S. Kite's translation (Vineland 1916; Internet Archive developmentofint00binerich), public domain; the French papers of 1905–1911 named beside it.

claim: The root doctrine: associations carried by vibrations — a physical mechanism of mind, stated as propositions. Every later learning theory is a refinement of this book's wager.
geplant: Selections from Part I (the doctrine of vibrations and associations, the propositions) from an early printing (Internet Archive observationsonma01hart, 1791).

titel: The Senses and the Intellect (1855) — selections
claim: Trial and error, and the ‘grouping’ of nerve currents that succeed together — the book read today as connectionism before the name.
geplant: Selections from the first edition (Internet Archive sensesintellectb00bain, 1855): spontaneous activity, trial and error, retentiveness and grouping.

titel: An Introduction to Comparative Psychology (1894) — selections
claim: Morgan's canon: never explain behaviour by a higher faculty when a lower one suffices — the founding rule against anthropomorphism, re-argued today wherever machine behaviour is described in mental terms.
geplant: Selections from the first edition (Internet Archive anintroductiont01morggoog): the canon and its defence, with the chapters that apply it.

titel: Comparative Physiology of the Brain and Comparative Psychology (1900) — selections
claim: The organism as tropism-machine: orientation to stimulus without inner life. The behavioural blueprint the first robot-builders read — and the hard lower bound of the automaton debate.
geplant: Selections from the 1900 printing (Internet Archive comparativephysi00loeb): tropisms, associative memory as criterion of consciousness.

claim: The law of effect: responses followed by satisfaction are stamped in. Reinforcement learning cites this book as its origin — the corpus's single most direct line into present-day AI.
geplant: Selections from the 1911 collected volume (Internet Archive animalintellige00thorgoog) with the 1898 monograph (animalintelligen00thoruoft) beside it: the puzzle boxes, the curves, the laws of exercise and effect.

titel: Psychology as the Behaviorist Views It (1913) — complete
claim: The behaviorist manifesto: prediction and control of behaviour, consciousness set aside. The psychology most ready to be mechanised — and the one the automaton debate warned against.
geplant: The Psychological Review paper of 1913 complete, from the journal's public-domain printing (JSTOR Early Journal Content / Internet Archive journal scans; exact item at ship time).

claim: The reflex made experimental system: conditioning, extinction, generalisation — the vocabulary in which learning could be written as procedure.
geplant: Selections from G. V. Anrep's translation (Oxford 1927; Internet Archive conditioned-reflexes-an-investigation-of-the-physiological-activity-of-the-cerebral-cortex), public domain in the United States.

titel: The Mentality of Apes (1917; English 1925) — selections
claim: Insight against trial and error: Sultan's stick and the detour experiments — the standing counter-evidence inside the learning line itself, and the ancestor of every ‘does it really understand?’ test.
geplant: Selections from Ella Winter's translation (1925 printing; Internet Archive in.ernet.dli.2015.187610), public domain in the United States.

titel: On the Hypothesis that Animals are Automata, and its History (1874) — complete
claim: The automaton theory stated at full strength: animals — and we — as conscious machines, consciousness a mere accompaniment. The debate about machine minds begins as a debate about our own.
geplant: The 1874 address complete, from Collected Essays vol. I, Method and Results (Internet Archive methodandresult01huxlgoog).

titel: Anthology: Are We Automata? (1879) · from The Principles of Psychology (1890)
claim: The great reply: consciousness as a fighter for ends, habit as plasticity, the stream of thought against the mosaic of ideas — the strongest nineteenth-century case that minds are not mere mechanism.
geplant: “Are We Automata?” (Mind IV, 1879) with selections from the Principles (Internet Archive principlesofpsyc01jameuoft): Habit, The Automaton-Theory, The Stream of Thought.

titel: Body and Mind: A History and a Defense of Animism (1911) — selections
claim: The last full-dress defence of the soul against mechanism before the machines arrived — carried as the debate's counter-voice, argument by argument.
geplant: Selections from the 1911 text (Internet Archive cu31924029080880, 1918 printing): the case against mechanistic psychology and the animist alternative.

claim: Forecasting human performance as a mechanical procedure: Hull's testing book already dreams of prediction done by machinery — the measured mind and the built machine converging.
geplant: Selections from the 1928 printing (Internet Archive aptitudetesting00hull), including the forecasting chapters.

autor: Clark L. Hull · H. D. Baernstein
titel: The conditioning machines: A Mechanical Parallel to the Conditioned Reflex (1929) · Knowledge and Purpose as Habit Mechanisms (1930)
claim: Psychologists build a machine that learns: Hull and Baernstein's electro-chemical model of the conditioned reflex, and Hull's argument that knowledge and purpose are habit mechanisms a machine could have. The corpus ends where the machines begin to learn.
geplant: The Science paper of 1929 and the Psychological Review paper of 1930 — the latter in the United States public domain since 1 January 2026 — from the journals' printings (items at ship time). The 1931 sequel (Baernstein & Hull, Journal of General Psychology) joins when its US term lapses in 2027.
